title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 10.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam went to Shechem
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:1.

questions.question: Who returned out of Egypt upon hearing the news in 2 Chronicles 10?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeroboam
questions.explanation: Jeroboam returned out of Egypt as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:2.

questions.question: What did the people ask Rehoboam to do regarding the yoke?
questions.correctAnswer: Ease it somewhat
questions.explanation: The people requested Rehoboam to ease the grievous servitude as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 10:4.

questions.question: How long did Rehoboam tell the people to return to him?
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: Rehoboam instructed them to come back after three days according to 2 Chronicles 10:5.

questions.question: Who did King Rehoboam take counsel with?
questions.correctAnswer: The old men
questions.explanation: Rehoboam took counsel with the old men who had stood before Solomon as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:6.

questions.question: What advice did the old men give to Rehoboam?
options: If thou be kind to this people
questions.correctAnswer: If thou be kind to this people
questions.explanation: The old men advised Rehoboam to be kind to the people and speak good words to them according to 2 Chronicles 10:7.

questions.question: What did Jeroboam do when he heard the news?
questions.correctAnswer: Returned out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeroboam returned out of Egypt when he heard the news as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:2.

questions.question: What would happen if Rehoboam eased the people's yoke?
questions.correctAnswer: They would serve him forever
questions.explanation: The people promised to serve Rehoboam forever if he eased their burdens as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:4.

questions.question: What did the people do after Rehoboam told them to return?
questions.correctAnswer: They departed
questions.explanation: The people departed after Rehoboam told them to come again after three days according to 2 Chronicles 10:5.

questions.question: How did the old men advise Rehoboam to speak to the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Kindly
questions.explanation: The old men advised him to please the people and speak good words to them as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 10:7.

questions.question: Rehoboam was in which location at the beginning of the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Shechem
questions.explanation: Rehoboam went to Shechem as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:1.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam was advised to ignore the people's request.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The old men advised Rehoboam to be kind to the people, not to ignore them, as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:7.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam was in Egypt before returning to Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeroboam had fled to Egypt and returned upon hearing the news, as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:2.

questions.question: True or False: The people were happy with Solomon's rule.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The people complained that Solomon made their yoke grievous, indicating they were not happy with his rule, as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:4.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam asked the people to return in four days.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Rehoboam told the people to return after three days, not four, as stated in 2 Chronicles 10:5.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Whose counsel did King Rehoboam forsake when deciding how to respond to the people?
questions.correctAnswer: The old men
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 10:8 states that he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 10:9 promise will happen if someone follows the advice given by the young men in verse 8?
options: They will speak roughly to the people
They will make the yoke lighter
They will seek peace with Israel
They will return a harsh answer to the people
questions.correctAnswer: They will return a harsh answer to the people
questions.explanation: Verse 9 asks what advice to give to return answer to the people, and the young men suggest a harsh response, as seen in verse 10.

questions.question: What metaphor did the young men use to describe how Rehoboam should respond to the people's request to lighten their yoke?
options: My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins
The burden will be shared equally
My hand will be gentle as my father's
questions.correctAnswer: My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 10:10 records the young men advising Rehoboam to say that his little finger will be thicker than his father's loins.

questions.question: How do 2 Chronicles 10:10 and 2 Chronicles 10:11 together illustrate the intended severity of Rehoboam's response?
options: They show he will make the yoke heavier and chastise with scorpions
They indicate he will lighten the yoke and offer peace
They suggest he will negotiate with the people
They describe him removing all burdens
questions.correctAnswer: They show he will make the yoke heavier and chastise with scorpions
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and verse 11 says he will add to their yoke and chastise with scorpions, showing increased severity.

questions.question: What practical lesson about leadership can be drawn from Rehoboam's decision to reject the old men's counsel?
options: Ignoring wise counsel can lead to harsh consequences
Strong punishment is the best way to lead
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring wise counsel can lead to harsh consequences
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's rejection of the old men's counsel led to a harsh response and negative outcomes, as seen in verses 8 and 13.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 10:12 show Rehoboam's attempt to manage expectations before giving his response?
options: He asked them to return after three days
He immediately gave his harsh answer
questions.correctAnswer: He asked them to return after three days
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows that Rehoboam told the people to come back to him on the third day before he answered.

questions.question: What attitude did Rehoboam display toward the people when he finally answered them?
questions.correctAnswer: Rough and harsh
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 10:13 states that the king answered them roughly.

questions.question: How can the advice of the young men in 2 Chronicles 10:10-11 be seen as a failure in servant leadership?
options: Because they suggested increasing the burden rather than easing it
Because they encouraged kindness to the people
Because they advised consulting the old men
questions.correctAnswer: Because they suggested increasing the burden rather than easing it
questions.explanation: The young men advised Rehoboam to increase the yoke and chastise with scorpions, which is the opposite of servant leadership's principle of easing burdens.

questions.question: What consequence might arise from the king's decision to chastise 'with scorpions' rather than 'with whips' as his father did?
options: It could cause greater suffering and rebellion
It would bring peace and unity
It would make the yoke lighter
It would show mercy to the people
questions.correctAnswer: It could cause greater suffering and rebellion
questions.explanation: The metaphor of chastising with scorpions implies harsher punishment, likely causing more suffering and resistance, as per 2 Chronicles 10:11.

questions.question: In what ways does the interaction in 2 Chronicles 10 illustrate the importance of humility in leadership?
options: Rehoboam's pride led him to reject wise counsel and caused division
Humility was shown by increasing punishments
The king was humble and listened carefully
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam's pride led him to reject wise counsel and caused division
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's rejection of the old men's counsel and harsh response (verses 8-14) demonstrate a lack of humility with negative consequences.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'my little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins' in 2 Chronicles 10:10 suggest about Rehoboam's leadership style?
options: It suggests a more oppressive and forceful leadership
It indicates a gentler approach than his father
It implies he will share power with the people
It shows he will be indecisive
questions.correctAnswer: It suggests a more oppressive and forceful leadership
questions.explanation: The phrase means Rehoboam intends to be stronger and more oppressive than his father, as indicated in verse 10.

questions.question: How does the people's request in 2 Chronicles 10:4 reflect their view of Solomon's rule?
options: They found Solomon's yoke grievous and want it eased
They were satisfied with Solomon's governance
They sought to rebel without cause
questions.correctAnswer: They found Solomon's yoke grievous and want it eased
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows the people asked Rehoboam to ease the grievous servitude and heavy yoke their father Solomon had put on them.

questions.question: Why is it significant that Jeroboam returned from Egypt in 2 Chronicles 10:2 when Rehoboam was made king?
options: Because Jeroboam represented the people's opposition and challenge to Rehoboam's rule
questions.correctAnswer: Because Jeroboam represented the people's opposition and challenge to Rehoboam's rule
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states Jeroboam returned from Egypt upon hearing Rehoboam was king, indicating a challenge to his authority.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 10:7, if a leader speaks kindly and pleases the people, they will serve him forever.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 7 explicitly states that if the leader is kind and pleases the people with good words, they will be his servants forever.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam accepted the advice of the old men and gave a gentle response to the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 10:8 and 10:13 show Rehoboam rejected the old men's counsel and answered roughly.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 10.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 10:15, why did the king not listen to the people?
options: For the cause was of God
Because he was afraid of Jeroboam
He wanted to please the young men
He was unsure of his decision
questions.correctAnswer: For the cause was of God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 10:15 states the king did not heed the people because it was God's cause to fulfill His word through Ahijah the Shilonite.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 10:16, what did the people say to the king when he refused to listen?
options: What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse
Let us go to battle against Judah
We demand a new king immediately
questions.correctAnswer: What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse
questions.explanation: Verse 16 records the people's response expressing no share in David or inheritance in Jesse's son, signaling rejection of Rehoboam's rule.

questions.question: Who reigned over the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah according to 2 Chronicles 10:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam
questions.explanation: Verse 17 indicates that Rehoboam continued to reign over the Israelites living in Judah's cities, while the rest rebelled.

questions.question: What happened to Hadoram, the officer over tribute, as told in 2 Chronicles 10:18?
options: He was stoned to death by the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He was stoned to death by the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that the children of Israel stoned Hadoram with stones, killing him, after which Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the lasting result of Israel's rebellion described in 2 Chronicles 10:19?
options: Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day
Israel was defeated and returned to David's rule
Rehoboam regained full control over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explains that Israel's rebellion against David's house persisted continually up to the time of the record.

questions.question: What was the purpose of God's cause in the events of 2 Chronicles 10:15?
options: That the LORD might perform his word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite
To punish Rehoboam for his harshness
To unify Israel under one king
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD might perform his word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states God's cause was to fulfill the prophecy delivered by Ahijah to Jeroboam.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'matnah' (translated as 'portion' in 2 Chronicles 10:16) mean?
questions.correctAnswer: A share or inheritance
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 10:16, 'portion' (Hebrew 'matnah') refers to a share or inheritance, fitting the context of the people's claim about their lack of inheritance in David.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in 2 Chronicles 10:14 where Rehoboam's speech contrasts with his father's rule?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Verse 14 uses antithesis by contrasting Rehoboam's harsher rule with his father's, emphasizing the increase in severity.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of division of Israel as described in 2 Chronicles 10:16?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:16-20 recounts the same event of Israel's division and rejection of Rehoboam, directly paralleling 2 Chronicles 10:16.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of rebellion against rightful authority found in 2 Chronicles 10:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 13:1-7
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1-7 emphasizes submission to governing authorities, contrasting with Israel's rebellion in 2 Chronicles 10:19.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the statement in 2 Chronicles 10:15 about the king not listening to the people?
options: Rehoboam's harsh answer to the people
The people's initial request for lighter burdens
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam's harsh answer to the people
questions.explanation: Verse 14 records Rehoboam's harsh reply, which immediately precedes verse 15 explaining the king's refusal to heed the people.

questions.question: How does the stoning of Hadoram in 2 Chronicles 10:18 serve as a typology in biblical history?
options: It foreshadows rejection of God's appointed leaders
It represents the establishment of a new covenant
It illustrates divine healing through suffering
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows rejection of God's appointed leaders
questions.explanation: The violent death of Hadoram foreshadows the continual rejection of God's appointed authorities, as seen in later biblical events.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'my little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins' in 2 Chronicles 10:10 employ as a literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Hyperbole
questions.explanation: Verse 10 uses hyperbole to exaggerate Rehoboam's intention to be harsher than his father.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 10:19, the rebellion of Israel against David's house ended during Rehoboam's reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 10:19 states the rebellion continued 'unto this day,' indicating it did not end during Rehoboam's reign.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Chronicles 10:15, the king's refusal to listen to the people was part of God's plan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says the king's refusal was 'for the cause was of God' to fulfill His word.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 10:4 teach about human sin in relation to authority?
options: Human sin manifests in rejecting just authority when burdened
Human sin is only evident in idolatry, not social grievances
Human sin is unrelated to political leadership
Humans inherently accept all forms of authority without complaint
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin manifests in rejecting just authority when burdened
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 10:4 shows the people expressing grievance over Solomon's heavy yoke, illustrating sin in rejecting the divinely sanctioned authority due to perceived hardship.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty does 2 Chronicles 10:15 teach?
options: God orchestrates human rebellion to fulfill prophetic promises
God is powerless over human kings' decisions
God condones all human actions equally
God's providence is unrelated to political events
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates human rebellion to fulfill prophetic promises
questions.explanation: Verse 10:15 explicitly states that the king's refusal to heed the people was 'for the cause was of God,' showing divine sovereignty over human rebellion to fulfill prophecy.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the consequences of rejecting wise counsel is taught in 2 Chronicles 10:13?
options: Rejecting godly counsel leads to judgment and division
Rejecting counsel has no consequences if one is king
Human wisdom is superior to any counsel
Counsel is only relevant in spiritual matters, not governance
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting godly counsel leads to judgment and division
questions.explanation: The king's choice to forsake the counsel of old men (2 Chronicles 10:13) precipitates the division of the kingdom, demonstrating the doctrinal truth about consequences of ignoring wise advice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 10:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 10:15 shows God's control over events by causing the king to refuse the people, demonstrating God's sovereignty over human history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially highlighted by Rehoboam seeking counsel in 2 Chronicles 10:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's consulting of the old men in 2 Chronicles 10:6 illustrates God's providence working through human advisors to guide decisions.

questions.question: How does the division of the kingdom in 2 Chronicles 10:16 prepare the redemptive theme of covenant faithfulness and judgment elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures Israel's later exile due to covenant unfaithfulness
It shows that political division has no spiritual consequence
It contradicts God's promise to David's line
It indicates that monarchy is unnecessary for covenant fulfillment
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Israel's later exile due to covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The rejection of David's house (10:16) foreshadows covenant judgment seen in the later exile narratives tied to Israel's unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is made by the people's rejection of Rehoboam in 2 Chronicles 10:16?
options: It echoes Israel's rejection of God's anointed king, anticipating the Messiah's rejection
It shows Israel's final acceptance of God's covenant
It marks the end of prophecy in Israel
It affirms the absolute loyalty of Israel to David's descendants
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes Israel's rejection of God's anointed king, anticipating the Messiah's rejection
questions.explanation: The people's dismissal of Rehoboam in 10:16 parallels Israel's recurring rejection of God's chosen leaders culminating in Messiah rejection.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 10 and 11 teach about human pride and the consequences of harsh leadership?
options: Prideful escalation of burdens leads to intensified rebellion and judgment
Harsh leadership always brings immediate peace
Pride has no impact on governance
Leadership severity is irrelevant to political stability
questions.correctAnswer: Prideful escalation of burdens leads to intensified rebellion and judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 show Rehoboam's boast about increasing burdens, teaching how prideful harshness provokes rebellion and divine judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 6 and 8 teach about the nature of wisdom and folly in leadership?
options: True wisdom seeks godly counsel, while folly rejects it for peer influence
Wisdom is always found among the young
Leadership decisions are best made without counsel
Folly is trusting the elders over youth
questions.correctAnswer: True wisdom seeks godly counsel, while folly rejects it for peer influence
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 8 contrast Rehoboam's wise consultation of elders with his folly in following young men's advice, illustrating biblical wisdom principles.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 13 and 19 teach about the long-term consequences of disobedience to God’s guidance in leadership?
options: Disobedience leads to ongoing division and rebellion against God’s ordained order
Disobedience is immediately forgiven without consequences
Division in Israel is unrelated to leadership sin
Disobedience only affects the leader personally, not the nation
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to ongoing division and rebellion against God’s ordained order
questions.explanation: Verse 13 shows Rehoboam's disobedience, and 19 records Israel's lasting rebellion, teaching the doctrine of persistent consequences for rejecting God’s guidance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 10:15-19 teaches that God causes evil by making Rehoboam disobey and Israel rebel. What does 2 Chronicles 10:15-19 actually teach?
options: God sovereignly permits human sin to fulfill his righteous judgment and promises
God directly forces evil actions without human responsibility
God abandons his people to chaos without purpose
God approves all acts of rebellion as good
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly permits human sin to fulfill his righteous judgment and promises
questions.explanation: Verses 15-19 clarify that God’s purpose is fulfilled through human decisions, permitting sin for righteous judgment, not causing sin itself.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is taught in 2 Chronicles 10:18 by the violent death of Hadoram?
options: Divine justice allows consequences for rebellion against rightful authority
Violence against officials is always condoned by God
God prevents all acts of rebellion by his people
Justice is irrelevant in political turmoil
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice allows consequences for rebellion against rightful authority
questions.explanation: The stoning of Hadoram (10:18) illustrates the consequences of Israel's rebellion against God's appointed authority, reflecting divine justice in history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly revealed in Rehoboam’s failure to heed advice in 2 Chronicles 10:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment
questions.explanation: The king's rejection of wise counsel (10:13) demonstrates God’s attribute of judgment against folly and disobedience.

questions.question: What theological synthesis can be drawn from the people's request in 2 Chronicles 10:4 and Rehoboam’s harsh response in 2 Chronicles 10:14 about human rebellion and divine purposes?
options: Human rebellion against burdens can be a means God uses to fulfill judgment and covenant promises
God desires never to allow human suffering under leadership
Rebellion is always outside God's sovereign plan
Divine purposes exclude human free will
questions.correctAnswer: Human rebellion against burdens can be a means God uses to fulfill judgment and covenant promises
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 14 show human complaint and harsh response, with verse 15 confirming God's purpose in allowing rebellion as part of covenant fulfillment.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 10:1 contribute to the narrative arc of Israel’s kingship and covenant identity?
options: Shechem as the assembly place highlights the people's role in covenantal kingship
Kingship in Israel is purely hereditary without people's involvement
Shechem was unrelated to Israel’s covenant history
The people had no part in choosing the king
questions.correctAnswer: Shechem as the assembly place highlights the people's role in covenantal kingship
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Israel gathering at Shechem to make Rehoboam king, emphasizing the covenantal relationship between king and people.
